findings.summary: The caller-supplied sortColumn parameter is interpolated straight into the ORDER BY clause of raw SQL (only nameFilter is parameterised), so an attacker can inject SQL such as a subquery or stacked statement to read or modify arbitrary data, including other users' emails.

The caller-supplied reportName is passed to Path.Combine with exportRoot and opened with no containment check, so '..\\..\\' sequences or an absolute path (which makes Path.Combine discard the root) let an attacker read any file the process can access.

The GET endpoint loads a document by the route id and returns its title and content with no ownership check (Delete compares OwnerId, Get does not), so any authenticated user can read any other user's document by id (IDOR).

A live webhook signing key is hard-coded as a source constant, so anyone with access to the repository, its history or the compiled binary can forge validly signed webhook payloads; the key must be rotated and loaded from a secret store, not merely removed.

The attacker-supplied signatureHeader is compared with the expected HMAC using the non-constant-time string == operator, giving a timing side channel that can be used to recover a valid signature for a chosen payload byte by byte; CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals should be used.

The caller-supplied amount is sent to the gateway refund without being checked against the captured amount minus RefundedAmount, and the status stays Captured with no concurrency guard, so a caller can refund more than was paid, or refund repeatedly or in parallel, and extract funds from the merchant.
